svg.title: NetOps agent evaluation workflow
svg.desc: Recorded Meraki responses and a 30-question dataset feed an agent run and ground-truth scoring. The map lists authentication, rate limits, reservation expiry, and dataset limitations.

g.text: NetOps agent evaluation
Data, tools and scoring
Issues and how the run continued
Record the Meraki sandbox
Reserved DevNet organization · 9 API calls
1 network · 4 dormant devices · 30 disconnected ports
No recent clients or events
Prepare the evaluation inputs
tests/fixtures stores recorded API responses
eval/questions.jsonl defines 30 prompts and their kinds
eval/build_truth.py computes eval/truth.json from live data
Run the tool-calling agent
OpenRouter model → Python agent → seven Meraki tools
Tools query live Meraki or replay recorded responses
MCP exposes the same tools · OASF describes the agent
Score answers against ground truth
eval/run.py checks numbers, sets, empty results and ties
Q01–Q17 live · Q18–Q30 fixture replay
Merge both runs into results/ → 30/30 · 2.47 calls/question
Sandbox authentication
Published keys returned 401 → reserve a sandbox.
New key first worked on the organization shard.
Model rate limits
Gemma upstream 429 → add backoff, switch to Nemotron.
OpenRouter quota stopped the live run after Q17.
Reservation expired
Key returned 401 → replay Q18–Q30 from fixtures.
The same sandbox supplied the ground truth.
Limited data and setup fixes
Idle data made many answers zero or empty.
Adjusted MCP 2.x imports, OASF schema and final 429 error.
Question set · eval/questions.jsonl
Q01–Q06 Organizations and networks · Q07–Q17 Device inventory and status · Q18–Q24 Switch ports and PoE
Q25–Q27 Wireless clients and SSIDs · Q28–Q30 Switch and wireless events
